Ashara gives a brief laugh, low and unguarded. “Enable him. I’d like to see how far he gets before the soup.”

Rashid’s mouth curves despite himself. “Rashid vel Amara. I do own a sense of proportion, however inconveniently.”

The fae woman looks up from her sweet. “He did say *tempted*. That isn’t an agreement.”

“Thank you, Thessaly,” Rashid says. “Your defense is very reassuring.”

At the far side of the table, the silver-haired elf closes her menu. “If we are cataloguing one another, do it before the squash cools.”

A server in Academy blue draws back the empty chair between Seraphel and Thessaly. A place card reads simply: **GARVEY**.

Rashid rests his furred fingertips beside his glass and looks directly at you. “Would you prefer the ancestry-and-voting-record version, or may we introduce ourselves like people?”
